rows.title: Policy divergence
rows.figure: Blackout: Oct hold ~85% locked; Dec the debate
rows.read: The Fed went silent Saturday — Goolsbee's Friday interview never produced a write-up, and October sits locked as a hold (~85% Friday) with December the live debate. ECB: no October hike priced, December 100%. BoC Oct 28 live (Macklem's hawkish lean plus WTI over $100); BoE Nov 5 on the GDP beat; RBNZ Oct 28 two-way; BoJ Oct 29-30. The new wildcard is trade: the Graham Act EO — armed, unfired, Oct 18 tripwire.

rows.title: Growth differentials
rows.figure: Week's scorecard final; China Q3 GDP next
rows.read: The week's growth prints are all in: US industrial production beat (+0.7%, sixth straight gain) while the NY Fed's October services index collapsed to -20.7 — factories up, services warning. UK GDP beat (+0.1%, 2.1% y/y strongest since Aug 2022); NZ manufacturing PMI 56.5, strongest since 2021. Next: China Q3 GDP (Mon), Canada CPI (Mon), US housing starts (Tue), UK CPI (Wed), NZ CPI (Wed).

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: Hot week stands; WTI >$100 the kicker
rows.read: Three hot prints in three days stand unrevised: CPI 3.7%, PPI +1.3% (biggest since Mar 2022), import prices +1.1% (+8.1% y/y, a four-year high — tariffs and energy feeding through). Eurozone CPI confirmed at 3.8% (three-year high, energy +18.9%). WTI back over $100 is the energy kicker into every October/November meeting; the Graham Act's Oct-18 tripwire is the next supply headline.

rows.title: Risk sentiment
rows.figure: Armed weekend: Sunday the double tripwire
rows.read: Saturday's wire split the Hormuz story into two tracks: Trump's claim of a Sunday signing (‘the Hormuz Strait is OPEN TO ALL’) vs Tehran's ‘not tomorrow’ — while the campaign broadened: IRGC claims two supertankers mined (unverified, Reuters-carried), UKMTO logs two tankers attacked off Saudi Arabia Friday and a foiled skiff approach on an LNG tanker off Yemen, and the WSJ documents Iran's targeting and intelligence support to the Houthis. Markets closed — no FX moved; Sunday is the double tripwire (claimed signing + the Graham Act's Oct-18 trigger).

rows.title: Terms of trade / commodities
rows.figure: WTI $100.71; Brent $109.28; spread ~$10.7 — Sunday open ~5pm CT
rows.read: Friday's closes stand: Nov WTI $100.71 (first over $100 in a month), Dec Brent $109.28 — the ~$10.7 Brent-WTI spread is the wide geopolitical premium. Saturday added campaign items (IRGC mine claims unverified, UKMTO Saudi/Yemen incidents, WSJ on Iran-Houthi targeting) and the first concrete off-ramp test: Trump's Sunday-signing claim vs Tehran's denial. Sunday's double tripwire — the claimed signing and the Graham Act's Oct-18 trigger — meets oil's Sunday open ~5pm CT.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: No new COT; funds long AUD (79th pctile)
rows.read: No new positioning data until Friday's COT. The flags stand: hedge funds net LONG AUD at the 79th percentile — the squeeze thesis is broken, so the pain trade is down, not up. Dollar longs mid-range (54th); euro 44th, yen 67th (less short than usual), franc 41st, CAD 31st — none crowded. DXY's first weekly fall in five is now testing the long-dollar book.

rows.title: Fiscal & sovereign risk
rows.read: The books stand: FY2026 deficit $1.992T — largest in five years (~6.2% of GDP); September's -$26.9B beat (-$34.7B fcst) but tariff refunds ($145B after the SCOTUS ruling) ate record customs duties, and debt service hit a record $1.36T. New: the Graham Act EO — +500% on Russian goods, +100% on top Russian-oil buyers from Oct 18, all waived for now. France: Oct 20 revenue vote, Moody's Oct 23; OAT-Bund 135.2bp.
